subject: Re: Sudden hosted API p95/p99 regression — request accumulation / batching fallout
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@playwright.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API — sudden p95/p99 degradation impacting inference latency

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in tail latency around 08:45 PT this morning. Our p95 jumped from ~220ms to 1.8s and p99 to ~3.6s for text-generation requests hitting model: redwood/gpt-small-v2. Throughput is unchanged but error rate has ticked up (502s at ~0.6%). This started coincident with a deploy on our side (longer context windows for some jobs), but the traces show request pile-ups in your hosted API (many inflight requests in queue for >500ms).

This is causing timeouts on our side and impacting customers in our beta. Can you confirm receipt and give an ETA for mitigation? We can throttle client traffic but need a short-term workaround and a plan to avoid recurrence.

Attached: a short request log excerpt and a screenshot of observed p95/p99 trend.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform — Playwright AI

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@playwright.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-18T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — sudden p95/p99 degradation impacting inference latency

Alex — thanks for flagging, we see the alert and logs and are on it. Quick note on next steps from my side: 1) immediate mitigations to reduce tail while we triage (scale workers, reduce max_batch_size, force routing off the contested host pool), 2) deeper RCA (look for batcher starvation / queue depth increase after your deploy), 3) customer comms and credits if SLA impacted.

I'll loop in Sean to lead the incident triage and Marissa for account communications. ETA for initial mitigations: 20–30 minutes.

—Rishi
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-18T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API — sudden p95/p99 degradation impacting inference latency

On Tue, Jun 18, 2028 at 09:28 AM Rishi Malhotra wrote:
> Alex — thanks for flagging, we see the alert and logs and are on it.

Quick triage notes:
- Observed behavior: request-accumulation in the batching layer. Batcher wait timers are extended for some shards because a subset of requests are being held open (longer client contexts). This increases queue depth and forces larger batch windows under our adaptive scheduler, which increases tail latency.
- Root cause hypothesis: a combination of recent model variant (v2) that has higher per-token latency at 1k+ context lengths and an upstream spike of long-sequence jobs from Playwright. The batcher policy hasn't compensated — it preferred throughput and allowed max_batch_delay to float.
- Immediate actions taken (09:35 PT):
  * Reduced max_batch_size from 128 -> 48 for affected model pool (expected to reduce batching-induced wait).
  * Temporarily pinned Playwright traffic to a larger but separate pool with extra workers (scale +20%).
  * Enabled per-request deadline enforcement at 2.5s to fail fast instead of building queue depth (short term).
- Short-term impact: should see p95 improvement inside 5–10 minutes; p99 may take longer while in-flight large requests drain.

I'll continue monitoring and will post sample traces/heap snapshots. If these mitigations don't sufficiently reduce tail, next step is to roll back to previous model variant for Playwright or enable a context-length cap on their route.

—Sean
SRE, Redwood Runtime

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@playwright.ai>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API — sudden p95/p99 degradation impacting inference latency

Alex — thank you for the quick heads-up and the logs. We're seeing the p95 drop to ~320ms after the emergency changes Sean put in (good early sign). A couple of customer notes while we stabilize:
- We will proactively apply a temporary context-length cap at the API gateway for your key to avoid new long-running requests until the pool finishes draining. This is reversible and targeted.
- If there's a business impact on your active sessions, we can provide a one-time service credit under SLA section 3.2. We'll finalize the calculation after the incident window.
- I'll schedule a follow-up call at 3pm PT to run through technical mitigations and long-term fixes (model pinning, batcher policy changes, route isolation).

Appreciate your patience — more updates in the call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@playwright.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, execs@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: batching/queue-depth-induced tail latency — Playwright AI

Team / Alex — quick summary and next steps after yesterday's incident (final update):

What happened:
- On 2028-06-18 ~08:45 PT we observed a rapid increase in p95/p99 for Playwright's route. Investigation showed request accumulation at the batching layer caused by a mix of: increased long-context requests from the customer and higher per-token runtime for the model variant serving them. The adaptive batcher allowed larger windows, which increased queue depth and amplified tail latency.

What we did (mitigations):
- Reduced max_batch_size and tightened max_batch_delay for affected pool; pinned Playwright traffic to a scaled pool; enforced short per-request deadlines to prevent indefinite queue growth.
- Deployed a temporary context-length cap at the gateway for Playwright's API key.
- Rolled back Playwright to model variant v1 for their route to regain pre-incident latency profile (agreed with Playwright during the 3pm call).

Impact:
- Customer p95 returned to ~240–320ms within 10 minutes of mitigations; p99 reduced more slowly and stabilized near 450–500ms after rollback. No data exposure; a small fraction of requests (~0.4%) received 502s during the peak.

Permanent remediation plan:
1) Add route-level batching profiles that consider context-length distribution (ETA: 3 weeks).
2) Auto-detect and backpressure long-sequence traffic to avoid batcher starvation (ETA: 2 weeks for gating rule; 6 weeks for full auto-scale behavior).
3) Improve observability: live queue-depth per-pool dashboards and alert thresholds (ETA: 1 week).

Customer-facing outcomes:
- We committed to a one-time credit for impacted window and a follow-up technical workshop to tune Playwright's usage pattern. Marissa will send the credit estimate.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll post a postmortem doc to the shared drive (link will be added to the HubSpot ticket).

—Rishi
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
